items.text: When the movie “Back to the Future” came out in the 1980s, people hoped that we might have flying cars in the 2000s, which we didn’t. However, at the 2023 Consumer Electronics Show (CES), a prototype flying car was one of the new vehicles on display. The flying car transitions from the ground to the air and you can try it through simulation; the company hopes that they will finish it in 2026. CES is an important tech event; this year, car technology was a focus with electric race cars, a large remote-controlled dump truck, and the flying car. BMW showed a kaleidoscopic concept car that could change to any color, while Honda and Sony showed an electric car with 45 sensors and cameras. Ram showed a concept pickup that will follow you if you get out, and Blackberry showed software to run devices in the car. Difficult words: prototype (the first version of a project or invention with all of its features), kaleidoscopic (an image that has many colors or shapes within it), concept (a project or invention to show if you can create something; the concept is before a prototype) You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In the 1980s, the movie “Back to the Future” showed flying cars, and people thought that we might have flying cars in the 2000s. We didn’t, but a company showed an early flying car at the 2023 Consumer Electronics Show (CES). The car transitions from the ground to the air, and you can fly it in a simulation ; the company hopes to finish the car in 2026. CES is an important tech event, and this year, car technology was a focus. People saw electric race cars, a large remote-controlled dump truck, the flying car, a car that changes color, an electric car with many sensors and cameras, a truck that follows you if you get out, and new software to run devices in the car. Difficult words: transition (to change from one situation to another), simulation (a model to show what something is like to use), sensor (a device that reads and collects information). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In the 1980s, the movie “Back to the Future” is in theaters. It shows flying cars. People think that we can have flying cars in the 2000s. We do not have flying cars for a long time. Recently, they become a real technology. A company shows a flying car at a show. The show is the 2023 Consumer Electronics Show (CES). CES is important for companies to share new technology. Car technology is the focus for this year’s show. Many types of cars are at the show. Some examples are electric race cars, a big remote-controlled dump truck, and the flying car. Other examples are a car that changes color, an electric car with many sensors and cameras, and a truck that follows you if you are outside the car. A company also shows new software for electronics in cars. Difficult words: focus (the main idea), remote-controlled dump truck (a truck that carries trash and a person controls it with electronics), sensor (a technology that reads information around something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Similar to the US riots in January 2022 for former President Trump, people rioted in January 2023 in Brazil for former President Bolsonaro. His supporters stormed government buildings because they refused to accept Luiz Inacio Lula de Silva’s election, just like Trump’s supporters didn’t accept Joe Biden’s election. Similar to Trump, Bolsonaro refused to concede the election, and people have been rioting for Bolsonaro since President Lula won the election in October 2022. Recently, Brazil announced it had control of the capital. The government and President Lula said they planned to punish the people involved, and police arrested more than 400 people who stormed the capitol, the presidential palace, and the supreme court. Unlike the US riots, no officials were in the buildings. Bolsonaro denounced the riots, and a Brazilian judge told the military to take apart camps of Bolsonaro supporters. US President Biden said that the country supported Brazil’s democracy and the peaceful transfer of power . Another government official said that the US must not allow Bolsonaro safety in Florida. The US government can remove a person’s visa, but Bolsonaro has a visa for leaders, which ends when a person’s leadership role ends. He came to the US before his role ended. Difficult words: concede (to stop a fight), denounce (to say something is bad), peaceful transfer of power (the change from one leader to another without war). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Similar to the US riots in January 2022 for former President Trump, people rioted in January 2023 in Brazil for former President Bolsonaro. His supporters stormed government buildings because they didn’t want President Lula, just like Trump’s supporters didn’t want President Biden. Similar to Trump, Bolsonaro refused to accept the election, and people rioted for him since October 2022. Recently, Brazil’s government said it had control of the capital, and it planned to punish the rioters. Police arrested more than 400 people who stormed government buildings. Unlike the US riots, no officials were in the buildings. Bolsonaro said that he didn’t like the riots, and US President Biden said the country supported Brazil’s democracy. One US government official wanted the US to make Bolsonaro leave the country. Difficult words: former (a past job or role), storm (to enter violently). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People riot in the US in January 2022. They are angry. They want President Trump to stay president. President Biden is the new president. The people storm government buildings. People riot in Brazil in January 2023. The reasons are similar. They are angry. They want President Bolsonaro to stay president. President Lula is the new president. The people storm government buildings. President Lula wins the job in October 2022. People riot since then. President Bolsonaro does not believe he should finish the job. President Trump says the same thing when President Biden wins. Recently, Brazil’s government says that it stops the riots . The people who riot are in trouble. The police arrest over 400 people. Bolsonaro says that he does not like the riots. US President Biden wants to help Brazil’s government. A US official says that the US must make Bolsonaro leave the country. Difficult words: riot (to act violently because of something that officials do), storm (to enter violently), riot (a situation when many people act violently). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

An Arctic walrus appeared in the British town of Scarborough over the New Year weekend, and it drew hundreds of spectators. The walrus named Thor had already been spotted in France in November and off the coast of Hampshire in early December. Thor’s surprise appearance forced authorities to cancel Scarborough’s New Year’s fireworks display over fears the event would distress the mammal. The walrus appeared to sleep at the harbor where he took a rest after his long adventure. Authorities put cordons in place to protect him from animals and people. Thor’s visit to the town came to an end when he inched towards the waterside, plopped in , and swam off. Difficult words: cordon (a line of persons or things around someone or something), plop in (to fall into water without a splash). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In November, people in France spotted an Arctic walrus in the sea. In early December, the animal appeared off the coast of Hampshire, UK. Last week, the walrus reached the British town of Scarborough. Although the animal spent just a few hours in the harbor, it won the hearts of local residents and tourists. They gave him the name Thor. Thor took some time to sleep after his long adventure , and then, he got back in the water and swam away. Local authorities canceled the New Year’s fireworks display because they feared that the event would disturb the animal. Difficult words: spot (to see someone or something), adventure (an unusual or exciting experience), disturb (to make someone upset or uneasy). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In November, people in France see a walrus in the sea. In December, people see the animal in Britain. At the New Year weekend, the walrus reaches Scarborough. Scarborough is a small town in Britain. The animal stays in the harbor . Local people and tourists are very excited. They name the walrus Thor. Thor takes a rest after a long swim. Authorities put a barrier around him to keep him safe. Authorities cancel New Year’s fireworks . They don’t want to scare Thor. After a few hours, he swims away. Difficult words: reach (to get to a place), harbor (a place near the sea where ships stay), firework (small explosives which people light and they make the sky full of colors). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The golden age of cocaine is after the time when Pablo Escobar was the drug kingpin ; it’s happening right now. People produce about 2,000 tons of cocaine every year, which is almost double the amount produced a decade ago. In Colombia, growers used around 200,000 hectares of land for coca last year, which is five times more than at the height at Escobar’s Medellín Cartel. The global fallout is showing up everywhere from the warehouses of Antwerp, Belgium, to coups in West Africa. The situation brings violence, corruption, and big profits. Colombian cocaine production began to rise ten years ago when the government started negotiations with the largest guerrilla group. However, when the guerrillas disbanded, new groups filled the areas that they occupied. The new groups threatened to kill farmers if they cooperated with government programs to eradicate coca. New Columbian president Gustavo Petro wants to stop the mafia and big shipments of cocaine rather than the poorest coca farmers. Difficult words: kingpin (a person that is essential to the success of an organization or operation), fallout (the negative result of a situation or action), eradicate (to destroy something bad). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Groups in Colombia make about 2,000 tons of cocaine every year, which is almost twice as much as they did ten years ago. Farmers use around 200,000 hectares of land to grow coca, the plant that creates cocaine. This area is five times more than in the time when Pablo Escobar was the leader of the powerful Medellín Cartel . Cocaine business has an impact on many countries, businesses and people, too. Ten years ago, the Colombian government wanted to destroy coca fields, and it negotiated with the largest unofficial military group in the country. The result wasn’t good. When the group got back its power, it threatened farmers to grow coca. The new president doesn’t want to punish poor coca farmers, but he wants to punish the mafia . Difficult words: cartel (an organized group of criminals from Mexico and South America), punish (to do something unpleasant if someone doesn’t do what they want), mafia (an organized group of criminals from Italy or other parts of the world). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Farmers in Colombia grow coca. This plant contains cocaine. Cocaine is an illegal drug. Colombia makes about 2,000 tons of cocaine every year. This amount is two times more than ten years ago. Coca farmers get only little money. The drug mafia makes money when it sells cocaine. The cocaine business has an impact on many countries and people. The Colombian government wants to change the situation. Officials punish coca farmers. They talk with military groups, too. The groups control the drugs. The officials cannot change the situation. The new president does not want to fight with farmers. He wants to fight with the mafia. Difficult words: illegal (against the rules), mafia (an organized group of people who do crimes), punish (to do something bad if someone doesn’t do what you want). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Long lines formed in the Bangladeshi capital Dhaka as excited residents waited to catch a train ride on the city’s first metro rail system. Last Wednesday, the rail network officially opened by the country’s prime minister Sheikh Hasina. People took six years to complete the first line, and Japan largely funded it; Japan is a major development partner of Bangladesh. The full network will encompass six routes and more than 100 stations, and people hope it will alleviate traffic jams in one of the world’s most densely-populated cities of more than 20 million people. Every hour, around 60,000 people will use the first line, and one carriage on every train will be reserved for women only. Difficult words: encompass (to include over a large area or many ideas), alleviate (to lessen a problem). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Dhaka is the capital of Bangladesh, and with 20 million people, it is one of the most populous cities in the world. Dhaka had no rail system in the past, and the streets were always full of cars. Now, upset residents hope that this situation is going to change. Last week, the first metro line finally opened after six years of construction. The first line is a part of a planned network of six lines and more than 100 stations. People often spent several hours to travel to work by car, so they were very excited to take the first train ride. Officials expect that around 60,000 passengers will use the line every hour. An official announced that one carriage on every train would be for women only. Difficult words: populous (a place with many people living in it), resident (a person who lives in a specific place), carriage (a part of a train where people can sit). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Dhaka is the capital city of Bangladesh. It is one of the most populous cities in the world. 20 million people live there. The city has a big problem. Too many cars are in the streets. Traffic jams happen all the time. People are upset. They drive for several hours to work. Now, this situation will change. The city has its first metro line. It can carry 60,000 people in one hour. People take six years to build the line. Japan gives money for the construction . The plan is to build five more lines. More than 100 stations will work for the line. Difficult words: populous (a place where many people live), traffic jam (a line of cars which move very slowly or not at all), construction (building things). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Former Pope Emeritus Benedict XVI died at the age of 95. He was the oldest pope elected in 275 years and the first German Pope in nearly 1,000 years. Benedict spent nearly eight years in the job, and he tried to reawaken Christianity in a secularized Europe. He retired on February 28, 2013, and his decision made him the first pope in 600 years to resign. In 2010, the global eruption of the church sex abuse scandal irreversibly affected Benedict’s legacy . However, as Pope, he did more than any of his predecessors and he changed the Vatican’s views on clergy of sexual abuse. He met the victims of priestly abuse privately and offered his personal apologies. After retirement, he only occasionally emerged from his converted monastery for special events. On Thursday, Pope Francis will lead Pope Benedict’s funeral in St. Peter’s Square, an unprecedented event in which a current pope will celebrate the funeral of a former one. Difficult words: secularized (separated from religious connection or influences), legacy (the long-lasting impact of a person’s life or events), clergy (religious leaders). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Emeritus Benedict XVI was Pope between 2005 and 2013. He retired in 2013 because of health problems, and he was the first pope in 600 years who resigned. Benedict XVI wanted to return Christian values to Europe, and he restarted several Christian traditions. In 2010, the world learned about sexual abuse by Catholic priests. This scandal affected how people looked at Christians and the Pope, too. When Benedict XVI retired, he only appeared in public for special events. On Thursday, the funeral of the former pope will happen the Vatican, and current Pope Francis will lead it. Difficult words: value (an idea that a person considers important in life), sexual abuse (force someone to do sexual activities), scandal (an action or event that many people consider wrong, and they are angry about it). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Benedict XVI is the pope between 2005 and 2013. He dies last week. He is 95 years old. Benedict wants to make Europe more Christian. He starts some traditions again. He does more than all the popes before him. In 2010, there is a big problem. People learn terrible news about the church. Catholic priests sexually abuse young men. This situation makes Benedict’s job difficult. The Pope stops his work in 2013. Since that time, he lives quietly in a monastery . Pope Francis will lead the funeral of Pope Benedict XVI. It will be on Thursday. Difficult words: sexual abuse (when a person forces someone else into sex), monastery (a building where religious people live and work), funeral (a ceremony which people hold when someone dies). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Around the world, people find solutions for climate change. Divers restored Cuba’s coral reefs by replanting bits of broken coral on nursery trees. Each handmade nursery tree can hold 40 to 50 coral fragments, and in one year, 400 fragments can create a barrier reef of 60 to 80 meters in length from only repopulated coral. Fields in California, United States, turned into massive ponds to store flood water in wet years and recharge the land during dry years. People rely heavily on groundwater; however, they must invest in water recharge when they can. A man from Tunisia compressed mine waste into bricks. These recycled bricks hold heat and save up to 50% of building costs. Santiago’s Mapocho River was a contaminated eyesore and is now a thriving urban wetland. After a decade-long effort between governments and local communities, the river now cleans the area and helps to control invasive species. Alice is an all-electric aircraft; it debuted its 8-minute flight. The plane produces no carbon emissions, and it significantly reduces noise and costs. Difficult words: recharge (to collect water so it goes deep into the ground), eyesore (an unpleasant or ugly sight in a public place), invasive (tend to spread quickly and difficult to stop). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Around the world, people work on climate change. Divers try to save Cuba’s broken coral reefs. They make artificial trees and attach small pieces of coral to them. In one year, 400 small pieces of coral can make a reef up to 80 meters long, and it has all the animals in it. In many parts of the world, people use groundwater. With long droughts , they must plan to store rainwater. In California, United States, fields turned into big ponds to save rainwater. When enough rain falls, people store the water for the times with little rain. The Mapocho River in Santiago, Chile, used to be very polluted. The government and local people spent 10 years to turn the river into a wetland . Now, it is full of life and it plays an important role as it cleans the air. Difficult words: artificial (something that people make), drought (a period of time when little rain falls), wetland (an area of very wet land with plants and animals). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People look for ways to stop climate change. Here are some solutions from 2022. Divers in Cuba want to save coral reefs . The corals are broken. Divers attach small pieces of coral to handmade trees. These trees turn into real corals. They grow fast. Fish and other small animals start to live there. People in California fight with droughts. A drought is a time with little rain. People turn large fields into ponds. When it rains, people store water in these ponds. They use this water when the droughts happen. The Mapocho River is in Santiago, Chile. The river is very dirty in the past. Nothing lives in it. For 10 years, people try to clean it. Now, the river is a wetland . It is full of life. Difficult words: solution (an idea to fix a problem), coral reef (a hard plant in the sea where many fish and other small animals live), wetland (an area of very wet land where plants and animals live). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Pele was the legendary Brazilian soccer player who rose from barefoot poverty to one of the greatest and best-known athletes in modern history. He recently died at the age of 82. Pele was the only man to win the World Cup three times as a player. In his glorious 21-year career, he scored a grand total of 1,283 goals. He transcended soccer like no player before him, and with his winning smile, he became one of the first global icons of the 20 th century. During and after Pele’s career in soccer, he was better known than many Hollywood stars or political figures who he met. The news about his death saddened the world; however, many Brazilians said that they were proud of such a genius athlete and great person from their country. Pele died in a hospital in Sao Paulo where he was undergoing treatment. His death was due to multiple organ failures from the progression of colon cancer. Difficult words: glorious (deserve admiration and praise), transcend (to rise above or go beyond a limit), progression (gradually develop to another stage). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Pele was one of the best soccer players in the world; he died on Thursday. Pele’s career as a soccer player lasted 21 years, and during this time, he scored 1,283 goals and won three times at the World Cup. He changed the world of soccer and became one of the biggest icons of the 20 th century. People loved him for his skills and his humble personality, as he loved helping others. He grew up in poverty , and he made millions of people proud to be Brazilians. Pele died from cancer in a hospital in Sao Paulo at the age of 82. Difficult words: icon (a very important and popular person), humble (a person who considers himself to be equal to others), poverty (very poor). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Pele is one of the best soccer players in the world. He dies on Thursday. He is 82 years old. Pele comes from Brazil. His family is very poor . He becomes a star. He is an important person of the 20 th century. Everyone knows Pele. His career in soccer goes for 21 years. He scores 1,283 goals. He wins the World Cup three times. He is the only person to do it. People love him as a person, too. He always smiles. He loves helping others. Pele dies in hospital in Sao Paulo. He dies from cancer . Difficult words: poor (have very little money), career (a job), cancer (a disease where a part of the body grows without control). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Holograms trained medical students and stroke victims used robotic legs; many life-changing health developments happened in 2022. Cambridge University Hospital and Los Angeles-based tech company GigXR developed an application called HoloScenarios to train medical students. It uses holograms to replace actors who pretend to be sick, which allow trainee doctors to assess patients’ symptoms and treat them without a hospital. The Da Vinci Xi robot helps doctors perform surgeries in South Africa. An immersive 3D console controls the robot’s four arms in real time for complex procedures such as colorectal and gynaecological surgeries. A driving simulator teaches teens with ADHD to keep their eyes on the road, which causes safer driving. Participants wear eye-tracking glasses that monitor head and eye movements, and they are alerted when they look away from the road for two or more seconds. At the start, they averaged 22 long glances away from the road per 15-minute drive. Months later, the number dropped to about 15 long glances in the trained group. Difficult words: hologram (a laser makes this image that looks solid or real), console (the control unit of a computer), colorectal (the body’s large bowel and its lowest parts). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In 2022, many health developments happened which could improve people’s lives; here are some of these developments. An application called HoloScenarios uses holograms to train medical students. Holograms act as patients, and students check their symptoms, and decide their treatments . They do this outside a hospital without real patients. Doctors in South Africa use a special robot to perform some of the most difficult medical operations. The robot has four arms, which a person controls by computer. People with ADHD can struggle to keep their eyes on the road while driving. A driving simulator teaches young people with ADHD to drive safely. Special glasses monitor when the head and eyes move, and they warn the driver if he looks away for more than two seconds. Difficult words: hologram (an image from a laser that makes the object or person look real), treatment (medical care for a patient), driving simulator (a device which looks like a car, and people can use it to learn to drive better). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Many great things happen in medicine in 2022. Here are some of the events. Holograms train medical students . Holograms are images or videos that look real. They look like patients . Medical students check if they are ill. Students learn how to care for the patients. They do not need to go to hospital. They wait to learn on real patients. Doctors in South Africa use a special robot. The robot does the most difficult medical work. It has four arms. A doctor uses a computer to control the robot. Young people with ADHD learn to drive safely. Special glasses check if they look on the road. If they look away for more than two seconds, the glasses warn them. Difficult words: medical student (a person who studies to become a doctor), patient (an ill person), ADHD (a brain difference which makes a person unable to sit still or cannot focus on one thing for a long time). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A deadly storm hit the US and paralyzed New York in deep freeze. The lethal storm is identified as a bomb cyclone, defined as a rapidly deepening area of pressure that causes severe ice, snow, and wind. The snowstorm cut power to hundreds of thousands of houses and businesses and disabled emergency response efforts. It left almost all fire trucks in New York City stranded. Buffalo is a city near the Canadian border, and it is one of the worst hit places. The blizzard blasted the city and is considered the worst in 45 years. The governor called it an epic once-in-a-lifetime weather disaster. At least 13 people died, and this number may rise as people find more bodies in vehicles or buried in the snow. Although the weather conditions in some of the hardest-hit areas improved, more snowfall may happen throughout the week. Difficult words: paralyze (to feel impossible to move or function), blizzard (a severe snowstorm with high winds), epic (exceptionally long and extreme). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A heavy snowstorm hit the US, and it cut power for more than 1.5 million people. The storm was a so-called bomb cyclone, which was an area of very low pressure . It extended more than 3,200 kilometers, and it brought ice, snow, and wind to some states. In some areas, temperatures dropped to -45 degrees Celsius. People burned clothes for warmth after they ran out of fuel. In New York City, all fire trucks got stuck in snow. At least 13 people died in Buffalo near the Canadian border. The storm was the worst in 45 years, and people died in their cars and in the snow. In some areas, the weather conditions improved, but forecasts said that more snow would come later in the week. Difficult words: pressure (heaviness of the air), run out of (to use all of something), forecast (an idea of what can happen in the future). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A heavy snowstorm hits the US. More than 1.5 million people lose power. The storm brings ice, heavy snow, and strong winds. Temperatures go as low as -45 degrees Celsius. People use all their fuel. They burn clothes to keep warm. A very bad situation happens in New York City. Almost all fire trucks are stuck in snow. They cannot help people. Buffalo is a city near the border with Canada. The storm is the worst in 45 years there. At least 13 people die. They die in their cars and in the snow. In some areas, the weather gets better. More snow will come later in the week. Difficult words: temperature (how cold or warm something is), stuck (not able to move), border (a line between two countries). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

2022 was a year of big milestones in space exploration. After multiple delays, NASA successfully launched its colossal SLS moon rocket and launched future moon and Mars missions. NASA’s 9-billion-dollar James Webb Space Telescope captured powerful images that opened a new chapter of cosmic exploration. China completed construction of its Celestial Palace space station, the second permanently inhabited space outpost after the International Space Station. In November, three Chinese astronauts arrived at the space station for the first in-orbit crew rotation in Chinese space history. Scientists unveiled an image of a supermassive black hole called Sagittarius A in the center of the Milky Way; it was only the second one ever to be imaged. Lastly, NASA’s Dart spacecraft successfully slammed into a distant asteroid in the world’s first test of a planetary defense system to prevent a potential meteorite collision with Earth. Difficult words: colossal (extremely large or great), outpost (an isolated or remote branch of something), potential (possible). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Many important events in space exploration happened in 2022. NASA successfully launched its uncrewed Artemis 1 mission; it was the return to moon missions and the start of missions to Mars. NASA’s spacecraft also successfully hit an asteroid and changed its trajectory in the world’s first defense system of our planet. For the second time in history, scientists took a picture of a black hole. They captured Sagittarius A, the black hole in the center of our galaxy. Amazing photos came from NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope which cost 9 billion dollars. Lastly, China built its first space station, and the first three astronauts arrived there in November. Difficult words: uncrewed (not carrying any people), trajectory (the path which a flying or moving object follows), capture (to take a picture or video of something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Many things happen in space exploration in 2022. NASA’s Artemis 1 mission starts. It begins missions to the moon and Mars. A NASA rocket also successfully hits an asteroid. The rocket changes the asteroid’s movement. This is important to keep our planet safe. NASA builds the James Webb Space Telescope. It costs 9 billion dollars. The telescope takes beautiful pictures. People see things which they never see before. Scientists take a picture of the black hole in the center of our galaxy . The black hole is called Sagittarius A. It is the second picture of a black hole in history. Lastly, China builds its first space station. First three astronauts arrive there in November. Difficult words: space exploration (send people and machines into space), telescope (an instrument to look at stars and other objects in space), galaxy (a system of millions of stars, gas, and dust). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

According to researchers at the University of Portsmouth, UK, the traditional roast Christmas dinner could have nearly a quarter of a million pieces of microplastic in it. Researchers cooked two different roast chicken dinners, one with all the ingredients wrapped in plastic packaging, and the other with no plastic packaging. They found about 230,000 pieces of microplastics in the wrapped dinner, which was seven times more than in the non-wrapped dinner. If someone ate a similar plastic packaged meal every day for a year, he would consume approximately 10 grams of plastic, which is the equivalent of two plastic bags. Unfortunately, microplastic-free food doesn’t exist because microplastics are in the air and in the soil. Global plastic production is projected to double within the next 20 years, and the amount of plastic waste flowing into the world’s oceans is projected to triple. Some people believe that if they avoid fish, they will not eat any microplastics; however, more microplastics are in our soil than in our oceans. Difficult words: equivalent (the amount or value that is the same as something else), avoid (to keep away from something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

British researchers found that when you eat the traditional roast Christmas dinner, 230,000 pieces of microplastics come into your body. Researchers cooked two roast chicken dinners and they compared the results. They cooked one dinner from ingredients wrapped in plastic, while the other dinner came in no plastic. The first dinner contained seven times more microplastics. Researchers found that if we ate this dinner every day, we would eat 10 grams of plastic. This amount is enough to make two plastic bags. Many people believe that if they eat no fish, then they won’t eat microplastics. This is no longer true because more microplastics are in the ground than in the oceans. Difficult words: microplastic (very small pieces of plastic), ingredient (any of the foods which make a dish). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Microplastics are very small pieces of plastics. We cannot see them. They are everywhere. They are in the oceans and in the soil , too. British researchers find how much microplastics are in the traditional Christmas dinner. They cook two dinners. The ingredients for one dinner are wrapped in plastic. The ingredients for the second dinner come in no plastic. The first dinner has a lot more plastic than the second one. 230,000 pieces of microplastic are in it. If people eat this dinner every day, they will eat two plastic bags. Experts say that in 20 years, three times as much plastic will be on Earth. People can slow down this problem. They can buy less things in plastic. Difficult words: soil (the part of Earth in which plants grow), traditional (something that people do for a long time without change), ingredient (any of the foods which make a dish or meal). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

After nearly a decade, US actor Angelina Jolie announced that she would step down as the United Nation’s refugee agency special envoy . During trips to Cambodia to film “Lara Croft: Tomb Raider”, humanitarian work sparked Jolie’s interest. She realized how some people received little education on the bad things happening in the world. In 2001, the UN first appointed her as a goodwill ambassador, and in 2012, she became the UN’s first special envoy. During her career, the Hollywood actor completed over 60 field missions from Burkina Faso to Pakistan, and she also raised awareness of sexual violence against women in conflict zones. In 2013, she received the Jean Hersholt Humanitarian award. Jolie said she was dedicated to working with refugees for the rest of her life, and she would work with organizations led by people most directly affected by conflicts. Difficult words: envoy (a representative on a diplomatic mission), humanitarian (improve people’s lives and reduce suffering), goodwill (kindness and support). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Angelina Jolie is a 47-year-old American actor, and for ten years, she was also a UN ambassador. Humanitarian work interested Jolie when she made a movie in Cambodia. She saw that people knew little about the problems in conflict zones and about refugees . This discovery changed her life, and in 2001, she became the UN ambassador. In 2012, Jolie represented the UN on diplomatic missions, and she worked in more than 60 of them. Jolie said that she would continue to work with refugees and she would work with organizations which help people in conflict zones. Difficult words: humanitarian work (help to people in emergency situations like a war), conflict zone (an area where people are fighting), refugee (a person who ran away from his country because it was dangerous). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Angelina Jolie is an American actor. She is 47 years old. For 10 years, she works as a United Nations (UN) ambassador . Last week, she says she will stop working for the UN. Difficult words: ambassador (a person who works for a country or organization), field mission (a trip to a dangerous area to help people there), refugee (a person who runs away from a country because it is dangerous to stay). By popular belief, the Christmas stocking tradition came from the legends of old Saint Nicholas. A family in his village had three daughters, and they were too poor to pay for their dowries for marriage. Nicholas was a generous man, and one evening, he dropped a bag of gold down the chimney or through a window. It fell into a hanging stocking which was drying. The next year, Nicholas gave the same gift for the second daughter, and the third year, he gave the same gift for the third daughter. The third year, the girl’s father stayed up all night to see if something suspicious was happening. Then the legend of Saint Nicholas spread. Over the years, the tradition has taken many shapes and sizes, from high-knee socks to boot-size stockings that many people hang in their homes today. Some countries often include an orange or tangerine in the toe to symbolize Saint Nicholas’s original gold gift. Other cultures leave shoes by the fireplace or outside their doors to receive gifts. Difficult words: dowry (an amount of property or money that a bride brings to her husband on their marriage), suspicious (questionable). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The tradition of the Christmas stocking likely began with the legend of Saint Nicholas. A man lived with three daughters, but the family was too poor, and the girls couldn’t get married. One night, Nicholas dropped a bag of gold down the family’s chimney , and the gold fell into a stocking that was hanging near the fire. The oldest daughter could get married because she had enough money. The next year, the same gift came to the second daughter, and the third year, Nicholas gave the gift to the youngest daughter. Then the legend of Saint Nicholas started. At Christmas, people hang stockings by the fireplace or on the wall. In some countries, people put an orange or tangerine in the stocking as a symbol of gold. In other countries, people leave shoes by the fireplace or at the door, and others put gifts inside. Difficult words: tradition (an action that people do for a long time without change), legend (a story from the past which many people know, but nobody knows if it is real), chimney (a structure inside a house which removes a fire’s smoke to outside the house). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Christmas stocking is one of the Christmas traditions . People hang it on a fireplace or on a wall. The tradition starts with the legend of Saint Nicholas. Nicholas is a very nice man. Three girls live with their father in a village. The family has little money. The girls cannot get married. One night, Nicholas drops a bag of gold down the chimney . Socks hang near the chimney. The gold falls in one of the socks. The oldest daughter has money to get married. Nicholas gives the same gift for the next two years. The two other daughters have money, too. Nowadays, some people put an orange or a tangerine in the stocking. The fruit is like the gold. Difficult words: tradition (something that people do for a long time without change), legend (an old story that nobody knows if it is true), chimney (a structure inside a house which takes the smoke from a fire to outside the house). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Farmers in Kenya fear GMO crops will undermine their livelihoods. After the worst drought in four decades, more than 4 million people are facing acute food shortages. In October 2022, the new government lifted a ban on the cultivation and import of genetically modified maize. According to officials, the change was necessary to boost crop amounts and improve food security. Organic farmers say GMO crops threaten the sustainable tradition to recycle seeds, and the crops will force maize growers to depend on foreign companies and owners of GMO seeds. Officials applauded the success of the technology in the country’s cotton industry; the industry had collapsed, but after the government allowed GMO varieties in 2019, the industry revived. Difficult words: undermine (to threaten), acute (serious or extreme), cultivation (the growth of plants for different uses). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In October 2022, Kenya’s new government lifted its ban on GMO maize. Now people can grow and sell genetically modified maize, which worries some farmers. They say that GMO crops can destroy traditional crops. Farmers will have to work big foreign companies because these companies have patents for the GMO seeds. The biggest drought in forty years hit Kenya, and official reports say that more than 4 million people have too little food. GMO maize could solve the problem, just like GMO helped another Kenyan industry. Cotton farms almost disappeared in Kenya, but GMO cotton helped farmers to grow it again and faster. Difficult words: traditional (an action that people do or use for a long time without change), patent (an official document that says who can make, use, or sell something), drought (a long time without rain). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

GMO plants are genetically modified. Scientists make things that are genetically modified. GMO plants grow faster or better. In the past, Kenya’s government doesn’t allow GMO maize. This situation changes in October 2022. The new government allows GMO maize. In recent years, rain doesn’t fall very much in Kenya. 4 million people have very little food. They could die. GMO maize can help them. Some farmers worry. They say that GMO maize is bad for them. It is bad for traditional farming. Big foreign companies have patents for GMO plants. Farmers will have to work with these companies. Also, organic farmers cannot grow plants near GMO plants. A 100-meter space must be between the plants. The space will make farmers’ fields smaller. Difficult words: traditional (something that people do or use for a long time), patent (an official document that gives rules on how you can use, make, or sell something), organic (food or farms without any chemicals). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Peru imposed curfew orders to contain violent demonstrations. The country has long-running political instability; the problems are reaching a boiling point. Since 2016, no elected leader has completed the five-year presidential term. Dina Boluarte is the running mate of the impeached left-wing president Pedro Castillo. The government swore her in as president on December 7, 2022, and she failed to end the anger, although she wanted to hold early elections. Since 2016, Boluarte is the sixth president. In the southern city of Ayacucho, Castillo’s supporters and police clashed, seven people died, and 50 more were injured. After a week of protests, the latest fatalities doubled the overall death toll to at least 14. Difficult words: curfew (a law that requires people to remain indoors between specified hours), impeached (formally accuse a public official of a serious offense related to his or her job), fatality (a death from an accident or violence). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

On December 7, 2022, Dina Boluarte became Peru’s new president, the sixth one since 2016. Pedro Castillo was the president before Boluarte, but the Congress of Peru removed him from office after officials accused him of serious crimes. Castillo’s supporters protested and demanded new presidential elections. Boluarte promised to hold early elections, but this change didn’t stop the protests. More than 14 people died last week. Last weekend, seven of Castillo’s supporters died and more than 50 were hurt in clashes in the city of Ayacucho. In some parts of the country, people must stay indoors between because it is too dangerous to be outside at certain hours. Difficult words: demand (to ask for something forcefully), supporter (a person who likes a certain public figure or political party), clash (a fight). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Pedro Castillo is the president of Peru. He tries to dissolve the Congress. Officials remove him from his job. On December 7, 2022, Dina Boluarte becomes the new president. She is the sixth president since 2016. Some people still like Castillo. They protest. The protests last for more than a week. More than 14 people die. Boluarte says a new election will happen soon. The protests don’t stop. Last weekend, protesters fight with police. Seven people die. 50 people are hurt. In some places, people must stay inside at night. It is too dangerous. Difficult words: dissolve (to break or make weaker), remove (to take away from a job), election (the time for people to vote a person for a job in government). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A huge aquarium burst in the center of a Berlin hotel, and one million liters of water poured from the 25-meter-high AquaDom onto a major road in the busy Mitte district. People speculated frigid temperatures cracked the tank and contributed to the leak; however, German police said they were still investigating the cause of the incident. Glass and debris swept out of the Radisson Blu, and according to police, splinters of glass injured people after the explosion. Around 300 guests and employees evacuated from the hotel. Before the incident, the aquarium was home to 1,500 tropical fish, and all of them sadly died. Fortunately, the incident happened at 5:45 am when hardly anyone was in the immediate vicinity . Difficult words: splinter (a small sharp piece of wood, glass, or similar material), vicinity (the area near a particular place). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Berlin, Germany, a big aquarium, cracked and one million liters of water poured onto a road. The aquarium was part of AquaDom, and a hotel surrounded it. Luckily, the incident happened early in the morning when no people were around. Glass and debris injured two people, and police evacuated around 300 guests and employees at the hotel. At first, people thought that the aquarium cracked because of low temperatures, but police weren’t were. 1,500 tropical fish were in the tank, and all of them sadly died. Difficult words: crack (to break), pour (to flow quickly in large amounts), surround (be all around someone or something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A very big aquarium is in Berlin, Germany. It is inside a hotel. The aquarium holds one million liters of water. On Friday, the aquarium breaks. All the water pours onto a road. 300 people must leave the building. Broken glass hurts two people. Luckily, the event happens early in the morning. Only a few people are around. 1,500 tropical fish are in the tank . They all die. The first reports say that low temperatures cause the event. Police do not know the truth. They must still find the reason. Difficult words: aquarium (a glass home for water animals and plants), pour (to move quickly), tank (a large container where people keep water, gas, and so on). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

US politician Marco Rubio presented bipartisan legislation to ban China’s social media app TikTok. The legislation would also block all transactions from any social media company located in or influenced by China and Russia. The action comes after a failed attempt by President Trump’s government to ban TikTok. Last month, FBI director Chris Ray said that the social network’s operations raised national security concerns, and China maybe could use TikTok to influence users or control their devices. Some US states have already banned the use of TikTok on government devices and computer networks. A TikTok spokesperson said politics motivated the legislation, and he said that it would do nothing to protect national security. Another bipartisan bill would limit access to US banks for Huawei technologies and other Chinese companies. Lawmakers said that these companies engaged in economic espionage against the United States. Difficult words: bipartisan (supported by two political parties), espionage (secret collection of information and reports on political, military, or business information). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

US politician Marco Rubio introduced a plan to ban TikTok.President Trump’s government previously tried to ban the Chinese social media app, but the attempt wasn’t successful. According to a government organization, China could possibly use TikTok to control its users and their phones, which could be dangerous for the United States. Some US states already banned TikTok on government phones and computers. TikTok said that the ban’s reasons were political, and the ban would not make the country safer. Another legislation plans to limit Chinese technologies and companies access to US banks. Difficult words: attempt (a try), legislation (a law or laws), limit (to control something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

TikTok is a Chinese social media app. Some US politicians want to ban TikTok in the country. Last month, a government organization says that TikTok can be dangerous. China can get information about TikTok users in the US. It can control their phones. Some US states ban TikTok on government phones and computers. President Donald Trump wants to ban TikTok when he is the president. He is not successful. TikTok says that the ban will not make the United States safer. Another legislation could make it difficult for Chinese companies to get to US banks. Some politicians believe that these companies want to get secret information. Difficult words: ban (to officially stop something), legislation (law), secret (something that nobody or only a few people know). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

On Tuesday, the US Department of Energy announced that scientists at the Lawrence Livermore National Lab in California, United States, achieved nuclear fusion for the first time ever. This is a breakthrough on fusion energy, the process that powers the sun and stars, and it took decades of research on the underlying technologies. The scientists focused 192 lasers on a target of fuel to combine two light atoms into a denser one to release the energy. This happened quickly, and for the first time in history, it produced more energy that the lasers produced. If companies can scale up the technology to a commercial level in the coming decades, nuclear fusion could one day slow climate change. However, more science needs to happen before fusion becomes commercially viable , and efforts to develop fusion shouldn’t slow down progress on alternative energy sources like solar and wind power, battery storage, and nuclear fission. Difficult words: underlying (basic, significant), scale up (to increase something in size, number, or extent), viable (capable of working successfully). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

On Tuesday, US officials announced a breakthrough on fusion energy. Fusion energy powers the sun and stars. In the process, two light atoms come together to make a heavier one, and this change releases a lot of energy. Scientists in California, United States, used 192 lasers to make a fusion, and for the first time ever, this work created more energy than the lasers required. If companies can use fusion to make electricity in the future, the situation could help the problems with climate change. Before this time comes, a lot more research needs to happen, and people should still focus on alternative energy like solar and wind power or nuclear energy. Difficult words: breakthrough (a sudden, important discovery), atom (the smallest unit of anything), focus (to concentrate on something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Nuclear fusion happens in every star. It gives the star energy. Nuclear fusion means that two atoms come together. They make one heavy atom. This one atom makes a lot of energy. Scientists try to make nuclear fusion for a long time. The research takes many years. The correct technology is hard to have. Last week, American scientists make nuclear fusion for the first time. They use 192 lasers for it. They make more energy than the fusion needs. Some people say that the event is the most important moment of the 21 st century. Nuclear fusion can make enough energy for all people. It will be clean energy. Still, the work will take many years before companies can use nuclear fusion. Difficult words: atom (the smallest part of anything), research (detailed study of something), technology (machines, equipment, and information which people use for a specific purpose). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Some 70 countries and institutions worldwide pledged more than 1.05 billion dollars in immediate aid to help Ukraine through the harsh winter. France hosted the global meeting to discuss what they could offer to Ukraine to maintain its water, food, energy, health, and transportation needs. Russian forces continue to batter the country’s energy and other civilian infrastructure. Foreign Minister Catherine Colonna said that over 440 million dollars will be for Ukraine’s energy sector . She added that the participation of non-Western countries such as Qatar and Cambodia showed growing support for Ukraine. The countries will channel the rest of the funds to other sector, and they will decide on how to use almost 530 million dollars. Difficult words: sector (infrastructure or industry), pledge (to formally promise), channel (to direct or guide towards a result). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

France hosted a meeting to help Ukraine through the harsh winter. More than 70 countries and institutions promised to send Ukraine more than 1.05 billion dollars between December and March. Over 440 million dollars will help Ukraine’s energy sector . Russian airstrikes damaged Ukraine’s energy grid and important infrastructure. The rest of the money will maintain water and food supplies, health, and transportation. According to officials, more and more countries supported Ukraine, and Qatar and Cambodia were among them. Ukraine’s prime minister said that he was grateful to all countries, and the help signaled that the whole civilized world supported Ukraine. Difficult words: energy sector (companies which make and sell energy), energy grid (power lines which move energy to buildings and homes), civilized world (countries with a high level of culture, science, and government). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

An important meeting takes place in France. More than 70 countries and organizations meet. They want to help Ukraine. Winter is very long and hard in Ukraine. Also, Russia destroys Ukraine’s power lines . People don’t have enough electricity and gas. The country needs help. Officials agree to send 1.05 billion dollars to Ukraine. This money will help Ukraine fix its power lines. It will also help get water and food to cities. A part of the money is for the health sector and transportation . This help will last from December to March. More and more countries help Ukraine. Ukraine’s prime minister thanks everyone for the help. Difficult words: power line (a big cable which has electrical power), sector (a part of a country’s activity), transportation (move things and people from place to place). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.
